_comment: Experimental: Orkeon Code on a Claude subscription, through the agent-cli provider of Orkeon (ADR-020 of Orkeon, ORKEXP010). The provider drives the claude command of this machine (the agent CLI of Anthropic, claude -p) signed in to its own subscription: install it, put it on the PATH and sign in once with claude /login. No API key reaches the CLI: Orkeon removes from its environment every ANTHROPIC_* variable and the three switches that send the CLI to a cloud vendor (Bedrock, Vertex, Foundry), and refuses, before any answer, a CLI that still runs on a key (Llm:AgentCli:RequireLogin). Meant for personal use, on the subscription of whoever runs it, and for any mode but docker: Orkeon 1.4.0 carries the provider, so the tool and source modes run it, and the docker image has neither claude nor its login. This example still needs ANTHROPIC_API_KEY: the Llm section is the default profile, the one of appsettings.anthropic.example.json, on that key; a session starts on it, and Orkeon's own services (planner, Guardian, judges) stay on it. With no key at all, write "Provider": "agent-cli" in the Llm section itself, with no Fallback. Llm:Profiles:subscription is the profile on the subscription. Its Fallback moves a call to the default profile, on the key, when the subscription is at its limit (Orkeon reads it as a rate limit), and also when the call timed out (TimeoutSeconds) or the CLI's stream broke. Copy this file to config/appsettings.local.json (ignored by git), then, in the REPL, /config set llm.profile subscription: every crew a command launches builds its agents on it. Llm:Profiles:subscription-haiku and subscription-sonnet are the same profile on the two cheaper models: with a decision model on the host, /config set route.ladder subscription-haiku,subscription-sonnet,subscription then /route on let it pick the model of each crew and sub-agent on the subscription, never above the profile the session names. Each of them falls back on the profile of its own model on the key, Llm:Profiles:haiku or sonnet as appsettings.anthropic.example.json declares them, so a launch routed to a cheaper rung stays on that model when the subscription is at its limit. To keep the conversation on the key and send the agents alone to the subscription, /config set agents.profile subscription instead: the turns stay on the default profile, the explorer they spawn and every crew a command launches run on the CLI. A call the CLI answered shows a cost of 0, the subscription pays; the CLI's own figure is kept as agent_cli_notional_cost_usd. A call that fell back is billed on the key and priced as such. Temperature, MaxTokens, top-p, the frequency and presence penalties, a seed, stop sequences, a response format, a grammar, a thinking budget, thinking switched off or switched on with no level, a level other than low, medium, high, xhigh and max, cache breakpoints, Llm:WorkspaceId and a tool call made required (ToolMode Required) do not reach the CLI: each is warned about once per run. At the Orkeon commit the sources are pinned on, a thinking level does (/effort, route.effort): the CLI starts with --effort, and a call at another level gets a CLI process of its own; Orkeon 1.4.0, which the tool mode runs, does not send it yet, and warns about it once per run as about the others. Llm:AgentCli sets how the CLI starts, at the runtime's defaults. The other sections are those of config/appsettings.example.json; see docs/configuration.md.
